# What Mason answers as Postgres does, and what it does not

> **The list is the code; the sentences are a template.** `tests/duck-gaps.test.ts` renders this file from
> `src/duck/gaps.ts` and `src/duck/verified.ts`, and CI holds it equal to what they render, so it is as current as the
> commit you are reading. To change the wording, edit the renderer; to change what is answered or refused, change the
> source; an edit made here is undone by the next `UPDATE_FIXTURE=1 npm run check`.

## At a glance

Mason is a drop-in replacement for a Postgres read replica: the SQL a tool sends Postgres is answered as Postgres
answers it — the same columns, types, values, text and order — or refused by name, never answered differently. Every
piece a statement is made of is verified against a real Postgres by the oracle ("What is verified" below names
each). The copy is read-only.

| Postgres | Mason |
|---|---|
| A `SELECT` over the copied tables (and the source's views over them): joins, subqueries, WITH queries, UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT, GROUP BY and grouping sets, HAVING, DISTINCT, ORDER BY under the database's collation, LIMIT / OFFSET / FETCH FIRST, window functions, CASE, COALESCE / NULLIF / GREATEST / LEAST, IN and ANY / ALL, parameters, EXPLAIN | answered exactly as Postgres answers it: 43 constructs and 87 forms of them verified |
| The types: "char", a type the source made, bigint, bit, bit varying, boolean, box, bytea, character, character varying, cid, cidr, circle, date, daterange, double precision, inet, int4multirange, int4range, int8range, integer, interval, json, jsonb, jsonpath, line, lseg, macaddr, macaddr8, money, name, numeric, numrange, oid, path, pg_lsn, point, polygon, real, regclass, regtype, smallint, text, tid, time with time zone, time without time zone, timestamp with time zone, timestamp without time zone, tsquery, tsrange, tstzmultirange, tstzrange, tsvector, uuid, xid, xid8, xml; arrays of bigint, bit, boolean, character, character varying, cidr, date, double precision, inet, int4range, integer, interval, json, jsonb, macaddr, money, numeric, oid, point, real, smallint, text, time with time zone, time without time zone, timestamp with time zone, timestamp without time zone, tsvector, uuid; the source's enums and citext; a table's row | answered (93 types verified) |
| Functions, operators, aggregates, window functions and casts | answered exactly: 256 functions, 387 operators, 95 aggregates, 58 window functions and 125 casts verified; "What is verified" below names each |
| Transactions, SET, SHOW, the catalog (`pg_catalog`, `information_schema`) and the protocol a tool uses | answered: what a BI tool asks at connection and before a query |
| Anything else: 55 shapes known not to answer as Postgres does ("Refused" below), and any function, operator or cast the oracle has not verified | refused by name (SQLSTATE 0A000), the error saying what to write instead; never answered differently |

## Why not DuckDB by itself

DuckDB reads most of Postgres's SQL, but does not answer it as Postgres does. The oracle's 6,233 statements,
each sent as written to Mason and to a plain DuckDB connection over the same copied tables (tests/integration/duck-oracle.itest.ts):

| Of 6,233 statements | Mason | DuckDB alone |
|---|---|---|
| answered exactly as Postgres: the rows, their text, the column names | 92% | 28% |
| answered differently by a decision the registry lists ("Answered differently" below) | 1% | — |
| refused, naming what to write instead (SQLSTATE 0A000, `Mason gap <id>`) | 7% | — |
| the right rows under DuckDB's own column names (`count_star()` for `count`, the expression's text for an unnamed column) | — | 20% |
| refused with DuckDB's own error (a function it lacks, syntax it does not read) | — | 20% |
| a wrong value (`7 / 2` is 3.5, LIKE's backslash escape, a float4 beside a literal, a numeric's rounding) | 0% | 13% |
| wrong rows, or the rows in another order | — | 9% |
| the same value in other text (`1.0` for `1`, a numeric's scale, a timestamptz without its offset) | — | 2% |
| another error than Postgres's, or answered where Postgres refuses | — | 9% |

A tool that reads Postgres reads the first row's answers; the rest it would have to work around, statement by
statement. The oracle's statements are adversarial by design (NULL beside '', ties, every type's edge values), so
plain reports fare better on DuckDB alone than this table says — and still not as Postgres.

## How a statement is decided

Mason answers a statement on DuckDB only when it can give **exactly** the answer Postgres gives: the same columns,
types, values, text and order (docs/DESIGN.md). Everything a statement is made of — each
function, operator, aggregate, cast, type and construct Postgres resolved it to — must be on the **verified** list at
the end: pieces a statement of tests/integration/duck-oracle.itest.ts used, which Mason answered exactly as a real
Postgres did, after a copy and after two rounds of changes. A statement using anything else is refused
(SQLSTATE 0A000, `Mason gap unverified`), and the error names each piece.

What is known **beyond** that list is below. A refusal names its gap in the error's detail (`Mason gap <id>`) and
says what to write instead in its hint.

## Refused (55)

A statement using one of these is refused with SQLSTATE 0A000, where Postgres would answer it.

| Gap | What | Postgres | Mason | Instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `generated-not-built` | a read of a generated table before its first build ended | a materialized view exists from its CREATE | refused with what the table is doing: being built, waiting for a table to sync, failed or refused | read it once it is built; mason status says how far it is |
| `unverified` | a function, operator, cast, type or construct Mason has not yet verified against Postgres | answers | refused, naming each piece | write the statement without it; report it to have it verified |
| `explain-option` | EXPLAIN (FORMAT XML), (FORMAT YAML), (GENERIC_PLAN) | the plan in XML or YAML; a plan for unbound parameters | refused by name: EXPLAIN is DuckDB's plan, in Postgres's text or JSON (docs/DESIGN.md) | FORMAT TEXT or FORMAT JSON; bind the parameters' values and EXPLAIN that |
| `set-config-forms` | set_config() anywhere but alone in a SELECT of no table with literal arguments: beside other columns or a FROM, in a subquery, with an expression, a parameter or NULL, under EXPLAIN | sets the parameter (for the transaction, under is_local) and answers its value | refused (SELECT set_config('name', 'value', false) alone is the session's SET, and with true its SET LOCAL, answered with its value as SHOW answers it) | SET name = 'value', or SELECT set_config('name', 'value', false) on its own |
| `star-join-twin` | a `*` of a named join (`(a JOIN b …) AS j`) with two columns of one name, sorted by an output of the two, or written out over USING, NATURAL or a GROUP BY | answers | refused (no name tells the two apart) | name the join's columns in the SELECT, or leave the join's own name out |
| `setop-ordinal-star` | ORDER BY a column number of a UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT whose first SELECT lists two columns of that name by a * | sorts by that column | refused | name the columns apart in the first SELECT |
| `with-ties-distinct` | FETCH FIRST … WITH TIES over SELECT DISTINCT | answers | refused (DuckDB has no WITH TIES; Mason's rank over DISTINCT is not Postgres's) | select the DISTINCT rows in a subquery and FETCH … WITH TIES from it |
| `collation-unknown` | COLLATE with a collation other than C, POSIX, default or an ICU locale the engine has | sorts and compares under it | refused | COLLATE "C" for byte order, or no COLLATE for the database's |
| `like-any-array` | LIKE / ILIKE ANY (or ALL) over an array that is not written out | answers | refused | write the patterns as ARRAY['…', '…'], or OR the LIKEs |
| `similar-to-forms` | SIMILAR TO with a pattern or ESCAPE that is not a literal, its substring markers, or substring(… SIMILAR … ESCAPE …) | answers | refused | a literal pattern, or ~ with a POSIX regular expression |
| `array-remove-type` | array_remove of an array of a type other than text, integers, floats, booleans, dates or timestamps | answers | refused | array_remove an array of one of those types |
| `json-agg-distinct` | json_agg / jsonb_agg (DISTINCT …) | answers | refused | select the DISTINCT values in a subquery and aggregate them |
| `json-rows-in-select` | json(b)_array_elements / json(b)_each in the SELECT list | a row per element | refused | read it in FROM: SELECT … FROM t, jsonb_array_elements(t.j) AS e |
| `regexp-flags` | regexp_replace with a start position or a count (its five- and six-argument forms) | answers | refused | regexp_replace(text, pattern, replacement[, flags]): flags g for every match |
| `regexp-functions` | regexp_split_to_table / regexp_split_to_array / regexp_count / regexp_instr / regexp_substr / regexp_like | answers | refused | ~ to test, substring(text from pattern) to take a part, regexp_replace to replace |
| `regexp-matches-forms` | regexp_matches in FROM | answers | refused | regexp_matches in the SELECT list |
| `json-of-type` | to_json / array_to_json / json_build_object of a value (or an array of elements) of a type Mason does not write as json | answers | refused | cast the value to text, a number, a boolean, a timestamp or json first |
| `extract-julian` | extract(julian FROM …) | answers | refused | extract(epoch FROM …) / 86400 + 2440587.5 |
| `with-ordinality` | a function in FROM … WITH ORDINALITY | numbers the rows | refused | row_number() OVER () instead |
| `array-subquery-element` | ARRAY(SELECT x …) whose x is a numeric, an array or a row; x = ANY or ALL (ARRAY(SELECT …)) | a numeric[] computed exactly, a multi-dimensional array (2202E on an empty element, 22004 on a NULL one), a record[] | refused (DuckDB makes a list of doubles, of lists, of structs; it binds ANY (ARRAY(SELECT …)) as a comparison of its own) | ARRAY(SELECT x::text …), array_agg(x ORDER BY …) in a subquery, or x = ANY (SELECT …) without the ARRAY |
| `json-path-type` | a json read's path cast to a type that changes its text (`varchar(n)[]`, `char(n)[]`, `name[]`) | answers | refused | cast the path to `text[]` |
| `multidim-array` | a multi-dimensional array literal, or one bound as a `text[]` parameter | answers | refused | a one-dimensional array |
| `array-lower-bound` | a `text[]` parameter whose subscripts do not start at 1 (`[2:3]={a,b}`) | answers, its first element at subscript 2 | refused | bind the array without its bounds (`{a,b}`) |
| `format-specifiers` | format() with a specifier other than %s (%I, %L, widths, positions) | answers | refused | concatenate with \|\|, or %s only |
| `to-char-patterns` | to_char of an interval or a time; its TZ, SP, EEEE, RN, V, B, L patterns; a day or month name padded to 9 characters in a parse | answers | refused | the patterns listed in the hint; extract(… FROM interval) for an interval's parts |
| `to-timestamp-format` | to_timestamp / to_date with a format that is not a literal | answers | refused | write the format as a string literal |
| `libc-uncovered` | ORDER BY, <, >, min / max of text (or of a jsonb, by its strings) holding a character whose order under a libc collation Mason could not read: under a locale other than English's (`en_*`, where it never is, nor is anything refused), a symbol with a first-level weight of its own (`㏩`, `㊿`) or any rare character the read was held to and differed on | answers, in the collation's order | refused when a value holding one is ordered (the order is read from the database, every character held to it, and glibc's every other character is followed) | ORDER BY x COLLATE "C" for byte order, or normalize(x, NFKC) where it spells the character out |
| `libc-locale-unread` | ORDER BY, <, >, min / max of text (or of a jsonb, by its strings) under a database whose libc collation Mason's read does not follow: a locale that tailors ASCII or Latin (tr_TR, sv_SE, cs_CZ) or another C library's. An `en_*` locale never is; the read says which at the start and mason status repeats it | answers, in the collation's order | refused whenever text is ordered; everything else is answered, equality, GROUP BY and DISTINCT of text included | add COLLATE "C" or an ICU collation (COLLATE "und-x-icu") to the comparison or the sort |
| `percentile-text-libc` | percentile_disc / mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY text) under a libc collation | answers | refused | order by a number, or ORDER BY … LIMIT in a subquery |
| `infinite-extract` | extract(year, decade, century, millennium, isoyear or epoch FROM) an infinite date or timestamp | Infinity (a numeric) | refused when a row holds one (DuckDB's DECIMAL has no Infinity) | filter the infinite values out (isfinite(x)), or date_part(…), which is a double |
| `time-date-trunc` | date_trunc of a time (Postgres truncates it as an interval) | an interval | refused | date_trunc of a timestamp, or extract the parts |
| `quote-ident` | quote_ident() | quotes an identifier when it must be | refused (it needs Postgres's keyword list) | quote it in the statement, or format('%s', …) |
| `div-numeric` | div() of a value that is not an integer | the integer quotient of two numerics | refused | trunc(a / b) |
| `jsonb-set` | jsonb_set, jsonb_insert, the #- operator, jsonb - of a text[] or an index | answers | refused | build the value with jsonb_build_object |
| `jsonb-compare` | a jsonb compared by GREATEST / LEAST, WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY …), IN or = ANY of a subquery or of an array not written out, BETWEEN SYMMETRIC, JOIN … USING or NATURAL JOIN, UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT (but UNION ALL), SELECT DISTINCT *, GROUPING SETS / ROLLUP / CUBE, or an aggregate's DISTINCT but count's; ORDER BY the number of a jsonb column a * lists; a row holding a jsonb compared, grouped or sorted; a jsonb[] sorted, grouped, compared, contained (@>, <@, &&) or searched (array_position, array_remove) | answers, by jsonb's own order and equality | refused (ORDER BY, GROUP BY, DISTINCT [ON], =, <, >, IN (…), = ANY (ARRAY[…]), BETWEEN, IS DISTINCT FROM, NULLIF, CASE x WHEN, PARTITION BY and count(DISTINCT …) of a jsonb are answered in its order) | compare the jsonb in one of the answered forms, a member (j ->> 'k'), or j::text for the canonical text |
| `text-array-order` | ORDER BY, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, min, max or <, > over a text[] under the database's collation | compares the elements under the collation | refused | sort by an element (a[1]), or by array_to_string(a, ',') |
| `sum-real` | sum() of a real (float4), as an aggregate or a window | accumulates in single precision | refused (DuckDB accumulates in double precision) | sum(x::double precision) |
| `interval-aggregates` | sum() or avg() of an interval | adds months, days and time apart | refused | sum(extract(epoch FROM x)) for the seconds |
| `bc-timestamptz-zone` | a timestamptz before year 1 written in a zone other than UTC | the zone's local mean time | refused when a row holds one | SET TimeZone = 'UTC', or filter those rows out |
| `width-bucket-forms` | width_bucket with its bounds reversed, or of an array of thresholds | answers | refused | low bound first |
| `inet-order` | ORDER BY, <, >, min or max over an inet | orders addresses by network, then host | refused (equality, IS NULL and the value itself are answered) | sort or compare another column |
| `held-type-compare` | what needs the type's own value of a column Mason holds as its text (money, bit, macaddr, cidr, a geometric type, a range, a tsvector, xml, a composite, an extension's type): ORDER BY, <, >, min, max, sum; a function, an operator, a cast to another type, a subscript or a field; GROUP BY or DISTINCT of a numrange, a tsquery or a tstzrange; = of a money | orders and computes by the type's own rules | refused (the value, x::text, IS NULL, count, and = and GROUP BY where equal values have one text are answered: docs/SQL-SUPPORT.md) | x::text, which sorts, groups and compares as text; or another column |
| `binary-held-type` | a column of a type Mason holds as its text, in binary format, but a point or a box | the type's binary form | refused | ask for the column in text format |
| `citext-forms` | GROUP BY, DISTINCT, min, max, a set operation, or = ANY (an array) over a citext | groups and sorts without regard to case, answering one spelling | refused (=, <>, <, >, IN (…), LIKE and ORDER BY are answered, case-insensitively) | GROUP BY lower(x), or x::text where case matters |
| `bytea-forms` | encode / decode to a format other than hex, base64 or escape, or one not written as a literal; convert_to / convert_from of an encoding other than UTF8 | answers | refused | encode(x, 'hex'), 'base64' or 'escape'; the UTF8 encoding |
| `row-value` | a row as a value outside the SELECT list, a cast to text and the json functions (compared, tested with IS NULL, grouped, sorted); a row of a row; a row of a table Mason synced in part | compares, tests and groups a row by its columns | refused | compare, test or sort its columns |
| `zone-abbreviation` | a time zone written as an abbreviation or a POSIX zone (`CST`, `IST`, `UTC+3`, `+05`) in AT TIME ZONE or date_trunc | a fixed offset (`CST` is -06 all year; `UTC+3` is three hours WEST) | refused, written or held by a row (DuckDB reads several as another zone: `CST` as Chicago's, `IST` as India's, `UTC+3` as east) | an IANA zone name (America/Chicago, Asia/Kolkata), in any case; UT, Z and UTC are UTC |
| `volatile-window` | a window ordered or partitioned by random() or another volatile function (a random row per group) | a new value per row | refused (DuckDB refuses a volatile expression there, and computes a deterministic one once for every row) | SELECT …, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY r) FROM (SELECT *, random() AS r FROM t) AS s |
| `numeric-special` | arithmetic on a numeric NaN or Infinity read from a text | NaN and ±Infinity by its own rules (NaN + 1 is NaN) | refused when a row holds one | filter the special values out first (x <> 'NaN') |
| `numeric-exact-sum` | sum() or avg() of a numeric Postgres's own function computes here — a text read as an unconstrained numeric (Metabase's JSON number, `(j ->> 'k')::numeric`), ln, exp, sqrt, power — holding a value of more than 20 integer digits or 36 decimals besides trailing zeros, or summing past 20 integer digits | adds every digit | refused when a row or the sum does (each value is summed exactly, in two DECIMAL(38,18) parts) | cast to numeric(p, s), or round(x, 18) first |
| `numeric-math` | ln, log, exp, sqrt or power of a numeric expression whose scale its types do not decide (a division, an unconstrained numeric's arithmetic) | digits at a scale from the argument's own | refused (a column, an integer, a literal and a numeric(p, s) are answered by Postgres's own function) | cast the argument to numeric(p, s) |
| `view-forms` | a view's whole row as a value (`SELECT v FROM v`), a WITH query named as a view the statement reads, a column qualified by its view's schema beside another item of the view's name, views read through more than 16 others | the view's row type; the WITH query or the view as each is in scope | refused (a view is answered by its definition in its place, as Postgres's rewriter answers it; its columns, `v.*` and `public.v.col` are answered) | name the view's columns; give the view or the WITH query another name |
| `enum-forms` | an array of an enum read from a text (`t::mood[]`) | reads each element as a label | refused (a column, a label, an array literal and a text read as one label are answered) | write the array as a literal, or ARRAY[…] of its labels |
| `infinite-interval` | an infinite interval read from a text (Postgres 17+) | infinity, -infinity | refused when a row holds one (DuckDB's interval has no infinity) | filter it out first, or read it as text |
| `relative-time-literal` | a relative time combined with anything else ('today 10:00', 'now'::date + …  written as one literal), or read from a row as a date or a time | the transaction's start (a row's value: when the row is read) | refused (a bare 'now', 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' literal is answered: the transaction's start at the Parse) | current_date + time '10:00', now(), current_date + 1 |

## Answered differently

19 cases are answered, but not as Postgres answers. Each is a decided difference the oracle checks still differs.

| Gap | What | Postgres | Mason | Instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fromless-text-order` | a SELECT of no table that compares or sorts text constants (`SELECT 'a' < 'B'`) under a collation other than C | the database's collation | the catalog answers it, in byte order (issue 141) | add COLLATE "C" to say so, or select FROM a table |
| `libc-mark-run-form` | text under a libc collation holding a combining mark written apart, then a digit or punctuation, then a letter that is a compatibility form at the third level (`ß`, `ð`, `æ`): `'a6ß'` against `'a' \|\| U+0308 \|\| '6ß'` | the mark's skipped run moves the third levels one along, and glibc compares a letter's with another's on one scale | reads each letter's third level as its own (a read of one scale asks the source of every letter), so such two values compare the other way round | ORDER BY normalize(x, NFC), which spells the mark in its letter, or COLLATE "C" |
| `libc-rare-letter` | text under an `en_*` collation holding a rare letter or symbol whose weights no spelling of it says, against the same word's near neighbour: `Ꜳ`, `Ꞛ`, `Ꞝ`, `Ꞟ`, an Arabic presentation-form ligature, a Tamil vowel written in two, a CJK compatibility symbol (`㏩`), a circled number (`㊿`, `⑯`) | the table's own weight | the weights the read could confirm: it sorts in its letter's place, and two such neighbours may turn round. mason status says how many pairs of those the read was held to differ | COLLATE "C" for byte order, or normalize(x, NFKC) where it spells the letter out |
| `limit-errors` | a value that raises (`'x'::int`, a bad JSON number) in a row a LIMIT leaves out: in the select list or a plain derived read's list (a view, a WITH query, a tool's wrapper), where no index gives the ORDER BY, a subquery of the select list among them (one Postgres finds cheap, it computes below its sort); or in the argument of a LEFT JOIN of a list's rows ON TRUE (unnest(ARRAY[…, 'x'::int]), jsonb_each of a non-object), under a LIMIT with no ORDER BY | the select list's raises: its plan sorts every row, its select list computed for each (through an index it stops at the limit and answers); the lateral's answers: it stops at the limit | the select list's answers: a sorted, limited select list, a derived list a join reads by row number, and a subquery in the list are computed for the rows the limit keeps (src/duck/late.ts), as Postgres's index scan does; the lateral's raises: DuckDB computes its argument for a whole vector of rows (2,048) before the limit stops it | none needed for the select list's answer; filter the bad rows out to have neither raise |
| `limit-lateral-filter` | a LEFT JOIN of a json document's rows ON TRUE (json_each, jsonb_array_elements, …) under a LIMIT, or a row count an Execute sets on the wire, and no ORDER BY, with a filter above the join that is not pushed down to the base: a WHERE on the lateral's own column (d.key <> 'n'), one holding a bound parameter ($1) in a SELECT around the join, or one in a SELECT that reads the join through a CTE | the first rows of the base, in its order, each row's members in theirs | the engine plans the lateral under such a filter as a delimiter join and hands the rows back in an order of its own, so the LIMIT keeps other rows (a filter on the base in the join's own SELECT, literal or parameter, or a literal one around it through a derived table, keeps Postgres's) | ORDER BY the base's key before the LIMIT, or filter the base in the SELECT that holds the join |
| `limit-lateral-argument` | a LEFT JOIN of a list's rows ON TRUE (unnest, json_each, jsonb_array_elements, …) under a LIMIT, or a row count an Execute sets on the wire, and no ORDER BY, whose argument holds a subquery (unnest(ARRAY(SELECT …))), or reads two or more columns of the row and no array (CASE WHEN t.kind = 'doc' THEN t.body END) in a SELECT whose list is a bare * or inside a join with a name of its own ((a LEFT JOIN … ON TRUE) AS j) | the first rows of the base, in its order, each row's members in theirs | DuckDB plans such a lateral as a delimiter join and hands the rows back in an order of its own, so the LIMIT keeps other rows (elsewhere an argument of two columns is computed in a step of its own before the lateral, which a * would read as a column; a subquery is a delimiter join in every form) | name the columns instead of *, or ORDER BY the base's key before the LIMIT |
| `window-partition-order` | a window function that reads its frame in order (row_number, lag, lead, first_value, last_value, nth_value, ntile) over a window with PARTITION BY and no ORDER BY | a partition's rows in the order its sort hands them back: in practice the order they came in | a partition's rows in the order DuckDB's partitioning hands them back, another one | ORDER BY in the window (OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY b)) |
| `mixed-scale-numeric` | a numeric column whose values have several scales: an integer UNION ALL a numeric, lead(x, 1, 0) beside numeric(2,1) values, an unconstrained column holding 1 and 1.50 | each value its own scale: 1, 1.5 | one scale per column: 1.0, 1.5 | cast to numeric(p, s), or round(x, s) |
| `unicode-16-case` | upper / lower of letters added in Unicode 16 | maps them (its own Unicode 16 tables) | leaves them as they are (DuckDB's ICU predates Unicode 16) | none needed for letters before Unicode 16 |
| `float-last-digit` | stddev / variance of a float, and ln, log, exp, power of a double: the last digit may differ | its algorithm and its machine's libm | DuckDB's and its machine's: alike on some pairs of machines, apart in the 16th–17th digit on others | round(x::numeric, 12), or compare within a tolerance (abs(a - b) <= 1e-12 * abs(b)) |
| `negative-zero` | -0 beside 0 in greatest / least / percentile_disc | keeps the one it met first | may answer the other | x + 0 makes -0 into 0 |
| `float-overflow` | exp / power of a double past its range, or so small it underflows | an error (22003) | Infinity, or 0 | bound the argument |
| `min-max-scale-tie` | min / max of a numeric expression (a quotient) where equal values have different scales (0 / 7 and 0 / 1000000) | the last of them it reads, so the scan order decides the trailing zeros | the one whose operands are least (min) or greatest (max) | round(min(a / b), n) |
| `numeric-stddev` | stddev / variance of DISTINCT integers or numerics, or of a numeric declared without a precision or with more than 18 digits: the last digits | exact numeric arithmetic, to its own scale | a double's 15 digits | round(stddev(x), 10) |
| `jsonb-equal-text` | GROUP BY or DISTINCT of jsonb values that are equal but written apart ('1.0' and '1.00', '{"a": 1}' and '{"a": 1.0}') | one group, written as the value its plan reads first | one group, written as the value DuckDB reads first: either may be any of them | GROUP BY j::text where the text must decide |
| `char-n-minmax` | greatest / least of a char(n) beside a text | compares without the padding, answers the first of equal values | compares the padded text | cast the char(n) to text first |
| `nested-exact-numeric` | an expression over a numeric a subquery computed exactly (a division, an avg, a round), outside that subquery: SELECT x * 2 FROM (SELECT a / 3 AS x …) | exact digits at every step | the subquery's value as DuckDB computed it (a double's 15 digits) where the outer query computes with it; passed through as it is (SELECT *, s.x), it is exact | compute it in the outermost query, or round(…, n) inside |
| `domain-column` | a column of a domain: pg_typeof(x) and information_schema.columns.domain_name | the domain's name | the column is read and declared as its base type, which is what the wire says and what information_schema's data_type says on Postgres too; a cast to the domain's name (`x::my_domain`) is 42704 | none needed: a value of the domain is a value of its base type; cast to the base type |
| `show-all` | SHOW ALL | every server setting with the source database's values | every setting the listener's catalog Postgres has, with this session's values laid over (search_path, TimeZone, ssl, …): Mason's settings, never your source database's | ask the source database for its settings (SHOW ALL or SHOW <name> there): Mason answers its own |

## Limits of the prototype (8)

Not about one statement: what the prototype cannot do yet.

| Gap | What | Postgres | Mason | Instead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `roles` | access | roles, grants on tables and columns, row-level security | a role (mason/roles.yml) grants a user tables and columns, held on the analysed tree and refused as Postgres refuses them (42501 permission denied for table …); information_schema and mason mcp list a role what it may read, pg_catalog still lists every synced column; a role's where: or through: filters a table's rows by the user's attributes (mason user add --set), every read of it filtered on the analysed tree and held by Postgres row security in the catalog behind a security barrier as a Postgres policy is (a statement's own expressions run only on the rows the filter keeps; timing is not guaranteed), a whole row or TABLESAMPLE of a filtered table refused, so is a grouping set relying on its key for a column it does not group, EXPLAIN of a statement reading one said in Mason's lines alone with no engine plan and EXPLAIN ANALYZE of it refused (either would say what the engine knows of every row), a user missing a value refused (42501) at every statement; a user with no role reads as mason/roles.yml's default: role, nothing when the file names none, every synced table when there is no file; a token reads every synced table | mason user add <name> --role <role> --set <attribute>=<value>; name the filtered table's columns in place of its whole row; read the full plan as a user with no row filter |
| `poll-full-scan` | keeping current by the poll (a table's sync: poll <interval>) | - | the xmin poll scans its table whole, every poll (no index covers xmin): ~13–17 s for 13 GiB | logical replication for that table: sync: replication on its entry (mason add <table> --sync replication) |
| `writes` | INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DDL, a read-write transaction | answers | refused by name: the synced data is read-only (a read-write transaction: 25006) | write to the source database; the synced data follows |
| `numeric-over-38-digits` | a numeric of more than 38 digits, or holding NaN or Infinity: a column, or a constant ('1e400'::numeric) inside Mason's arithmetic or a WHERE | exact | a double (15 digits), said in the log for a column; a constant the outermost SELECT answers is exact | numeric(p, s) with p ≤ 38 |
| `numeric-array` | an unconstrained numeric[] column | exact elements | double precision elements (15 digits), said in the log | numeric(p, s)[] |
| `numeric-parameter` | a numeric parameter ($1) compared in a WHERE | exact | a double (exact to 15 digits) | a literal |
| `spill-limit` | a statement that spills more to disk than Mason keeps for statements: a sort, a join or an aggregate past the memory limit | spills up to temp_file_limit, or until the disk is full | fails alone with 53400 past half of the disk's room, what is free and what statements have spilled (or MASON_SPILL_LIMIT), so the sync keeps room to write; a disk that is really full is 53100 | ask for less at once (a filter, a LIMIT, fewer or narrower columns), free disk, or raise MASON_SPILL_LIMIT |
| `log-literals` | .mason/mason.log's statement lines | - | each statement DuckDB ran, whole, literals included | keep the log private |
